name: FC Vaduz
content:
FC Vaduz is a professional football club based in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, founded in 1932. It is the most prominent and successful club in the country and plays in the Swiss football league system because Liechtenstein does not have its own national league. The team has competed in various tiers of Swiss football, including the Super League, and plays its home matches at the Rheinpark Stadion.

Domestically, FC Vaduz has dominated the Liechtenstein Football Cup, winning it dozens of times and holding a world record for the most domestic cup victories. Because the cup is the only national competition, it serves as the club’s main route to European tournaments. Vaduz has regularly qualified for UEFA competitions and achieved notable milestones, including reaching the group stage of the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2022, becoming the first club from Liechtenstein to do so.

Despite its domestic dominance, the club’s performance in the Swiss league system has been more modest, with periods of promotion to and relegation from the top division. Its best achievements include winning the Swiss Challenge League and earning promotion to the Super League, where it has competed intermittently. Today, FC Vaduz remains the leading football institution in Liechtenstein, combining domestic success with participation in a foreign league system.

name: FC Balzers
content:
FC Balzers is a football club from the municipality of Balzers in Liechtenstein, founded in 1932. It is one of the oldest and most important clubs in the country and was the first Liechtenstein team to join the Swiss Football Association. Like all clubs from Liechtenstein, it competes in the Swiss league system while also participating in the Liechtenstein Football Cup, which serves as the country’s main domestic competition.

The club has been one of the most successful teams in Liechtenstein, winning the national cup 11 times and ranking as the second most successful club in the competition’s history after FC Vaduz. Its most dominant period came between the late 1970s and early 1980s, when it won multiple cup titles in a short span. FC Balzers also achieved promotions within the Swiss league system, reaching higher amateur levels and maintaining a strong presence over decades.

On the international stage, FC Balzers has participated in European competitions through its cup victories. The club made history in 1993 by becoming the first team from Liechtenstein to win a tie in European competition, reaching the main round of the Cup Winners’ Cup. Although it never achieved major success in Europe, FC Balzers remains an important club in Liechtenstein football, known for its tradition, cup success, and role in developing players from the country.

name: FC Triesen
content:
FC Triesen is a Liechtenstein football club based in the municipality of Triesen, founded in 1932. It is one of the seven official football clubs in the country and plays its home matches at the Sportanlage Blumenau. Like all Liechtenstein teams, FC Triesen competes in the Swiss football league system, currently playing in the lower tiers, while also taking part in the national cup competition.

The club was one of the pioneers of football in Liechtenstein and enjoyed early success in domestic competitions. It won the Liechtenstein championship three times in the 1930s, during a period when a local championship format existed. FC Triesen also became one of the most successful teams in the Liechtenstein Football Cup, winning the tournament eight times, mainly between the 1940s and 1970s.

In modern times, FC Triesen has remained an important but more modest club within Liechtenstein football. It continues to compete regularly in the national cup and the Swiss league system, focusing on maintaining its football tradition and developing local players. Although it no longer dominates domestically, it is still considered one of the historic clubs in Liechtenstein football.

name: USV Eschen/Mauren
content:
USV Eschen/Mauren is a Liechtenstein football club based in the municipalities of Eschen and Mauren, founded in 1963 through the merger of FC Eschen and FC Mauren. The club plays its home matches at the Sportpark Eschen-Mauren, which previously served as the national stadium of Liechtenstein before the construction of Rheinpark Stadion. Like all clubs from Liechtenstein, it competes in the Swiss football league system, currently playing in the lower tiers.

Throughout its history, USV Eschen/Mauren has mostly played in the regional levels of Swiss football, with occasional promotions to higher divisions such as the 1. Liga. The club has generally maintained a stable presence in the lower leagues, focusing on long-term participation rather than major breakthroughs at the national league level. Its structure reflects the typical situation of Liechtenstein clubs, which depend on the Swiss system due to the absence of a domestic league.

The club has enjoyed its greatest success in the Liechtenstein Football Cup, winning the competition five times, including three consecutive titles in the 1970s and its most recent victory in 2012. It has also been a frequent runner-up, reaching the final numerous times. Thanks to its cup success, USV Eschen/Mauren has participated in European competitions, although without progressing beyond the early qualifying rounds.

name: FC Schaan
content:
FC Schaan is a Liechtenstein football club based in the municipality of Schaan, founded in 1949. It is one of the seven official clubs in the country and plays its home matches at the Sportplatz Rheinwiese. Like all Liechtenstein teams, it competes in the Swiss football league system, currently in the lower tiers, while also participating annually in the national cup competition.

The club has a long tradition in Liechtenstein football and achieved its greatest success in the national cup, winning the Liechtenstein Football Cup three times (1955, 1963, and 1994). It has also been a frequent finalist, finishing as runner-up on multiple occasions. In 1994, this cup victory allowed FC Schaan to compete in European competition for the first time, although it was eliminated in the qualifying round.

Throughout its history, FC Schaan has mainly played in the lower divisions of Swiss football, focusing on stability and local player development. The club maintains a youth system in cooperation with FC Vaduz, contributing to football development in the country. Although it has not been a dominant force in recent years, FC Schaan remains an important historic club in Liechtenstein football.

name: FC Ruggell
content:
FC Ruggell is a Liechtenstein football club based in the municipality of Ruggell, founded in 1958. It is an amateur team that competes in the Swiss football league system, as Liechtenstein does not have its own national league. The club plays its home matches at the Freizeitpark Widau and represents one of the smaller but established football institutions in the country.

Throughout its history, FC Ruggell has mainly played in the lower divisions of Swiss football, moving between levels such as the 3rd and 4th Liga before eventually reaching the 2. Liga. The club experienced periods of promotion and relegation but remained a stable participant in regional competitions. In addition to league play, it has occasionally achieved notable results in the Swiss Cup and developed youth teams with some success over the years.

The club’s most significant achievements have come in the Liechtenstein Football Cup, where it has reached the final seven times, although it has never won the competition. Its most recent final appearance was in 2019, when it narrowly lost to FC Vaduz. Despite limited success in winning trophies, FC Ruggell remains an important part of Liechtenstein football, contributing to the local sporting culture and development of players.

name: FC Triesenberg
content:
FC Triesenberg is a Liechtenstein amateur football club based in the municipality of Triesenberg, founded in 1972. Like all Liechtenstein teams, the club competes in the Swiss football league system due to the absence of a national league, currently playing in the lower divisions.

Throughout its history, FC Triesenberg has mainly competed in the Swiss lower leagues, beginning in the 4th tier and gradually achieving promotions. The club first reached the 3. Liga in the 1986–87 season and later experienced periods of relegation and promotion, including a return to the 3rd level in 2001 and a brief promotion to the 2. Liga in 2010. Despite these fluctuations, it has remained a stable amateur side focused on local football development.

In domestic competition, FC Triesenberg participates annually in the Liechtenstein Football Cup, which is the country’s main tournament. The club has never won the competition but achieved its best results by reaching the final in 2015 and again in 2024. Although it has not secured major trophies, FC Triesenberg remains an important part of Liechtenstein football, contributing to the country’s football structure and local sporting culture.
